newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Philip Morris Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Philip Morris Q1 results.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said profits rose to $0.73 a share in the first quarter compared to $0.63 last year on Wednesday, matching analysts' estimates.
The following is the full text statement of the company's press release.
NEW YORK, April 16 - Highlights of 1997 first-quarter earnings:
E.P.S. up 15.9% to record $0.73 per share

- Philip Morris earned a record $0.73 per share in the first quarter, up 15.9%, and net earnings rose 13.3%, to $1.8 billion -- another record high. The gains were fueled by strong results from the company's domestic and international tobacco businesses and its North American food business.
- Income from operations rose 11.3%, to $3.5 billion, on revenues of $18.2 billion, up 4.6% from 1996, excluding North American food businesses divested since the beginning of 1996.
- Domestic Tobacco: The company's domestic tobacco business enjoyed another outstanding quarter, earning $1.1 billion, 10.6% higher than last year, on revenues of $2.9 billion, up 2.8%.

- International Tobacco: First-quarter results were again excellent. Income climbed 15.0% on record volume, up 8.5%, as the business continued to benefit from the overseas popularity of its American-style cigarettes.

- North American Food: North American Food turned in a superb quarter with income up 10.1% on strong volume gains in all U.S. retail businesses. - International Food: International food recorded income growth of 3.8% on volume gains in Europe and continued cost reductions.
- Beer: Income was up 2.6% due to continued productivity improvements and lower costs.
- During the quarter, the company announced a three-for-one stock split and a 3-year, $8 billion share repurchase program.

Philip Morris Companies Inc. (NYSE: MO) continued its profit momentum in the first quarter as net earnings per share climbed 15.9%, to a record $0.73, and net earnings rose 13.3%, to $1.8 billion -- another record high. Income from operations in the first quarter grew 11.3%, to $3.5 billion, on operating revenues of $18.2 billion, 4.6% higher than last year.

The company continued to deliver solid earnings growth, led by strong results from both its domestic and international tobacco businesses and its North American food business. Performance was robust despite the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against key foreign currencies.

"The Philip Morris growth machine is steaming ahead," said Geoffrey C. Bible, chairman of the board and chief executive officer. "Although we will have to continue to contend with the strengthening of the U.S. dollar, the volume, market share and earnings fundamentals of our businesses remain powerful."
Delivering Shareholder Value

During the quarter, Philip Morris took further steps to enhance shareholder value. The company announced a three-for-one stock split for shareholders of record on March 17, 1997. Including this split, the company's common stock has been split seven times since January 1, 1966, with the result that one share in 1966 is now the equivalent of 576 shares.

In February, the company also announced a new 3-year, $8 billion share repurchase program. This program follows a 3-year, $6 billion program that was completed on April 2, 1997. The following review of the company's performance refers to first-quarter 1997 results compared with those of the year-earlier period. For the company's worldwide food business, results of operations exclude North American food businesses divested since the beginning of 1996. TOBACCO

Income from worldwide tobacco operations climbed 13.0%, to $2.4 billion, on revenues of $9.9 billion, 8.5% higher than last year. During the quarter, Philip Morris sold 244 billion cigarettes, 6.3% more than in 1996. Worldwide volume for the Marlboro brand climbed 4.9%.
Domestic Tobacco

Philip Morris Incorporated (PM USA), the company's domestic tobacco business, enjoyed another outstanding quarter, earning $1.1 billion, 10.6% higher than last year, on operating revenues of $2.9 billion, up 2.8%. The gains were driven by margin improvements and a continued shift in sales to more profitable premium brands.

PM USA's shipments of 53.4 billion cigarettes were down 1.0%, due in part to one less shipping day. Industry volume declined 2.9% in the quarter, partially for the same reason. PM USA's total share of industry shipments climbed 0.9 percentage points to a record 48.7%.

Volume for Marlboro, the top-selling cigarette brand in the U.S., continued to increase, growing 1.5%, to 36.8 billion cigarettes, and the brand added 1.5 share points to capture a record 33.5% of industry volume.

PM USA's share of the premium segment increased to 57.5%, up 1.4 points from the prior year. Higher-margin, premium cigarettes accounted for 84.6% of the operating company's total shipment volume, a full percentage point more than last year.

As a group, PM USA's other premium brands, which include Merit, Benson & Hedges, Parliament and Virginia Slims, accounted for 7.7% of industry shipments, down 0.2 share points from last year's first quarter. Basic held its 5.0% share of industry shipments, and its share of the declining discount segment advanced 0.5 points, to 17.7%.

Consumer purchases as measured by retail data from A.C. Nielsen Company are consistent with these shipment trends. At retail, a record 50.3% of cigarettes sold were Philip Morris brands, 1.6 share points higher than last year. In addition, Marlboro's retail share rose 2.0 share points to a record 34.4%.
International Tobacco

The tobacco business of Philip Morris International Inc. (PMI) achieved excellent results for the first quarter, continuing to build on its solid, global business momentum, with strong gains in income, revenues and volume. Operating income of $1.3 billion was 15.0% higher than last year, on revenues of $7.0 billion, up 11.0%. The gains were driven by higher volume and pricing, partially offset by unfavorable currency reflecting the strengthening of the U.S. dollar, principally versus the Japanese yen and European currencies. PMI sold 191 billion cigarettes in the quarter, up 8.5%, led by an 8.3% increase in the volume of its profitable portfolio of leading U.S.-heritage and international brands -- Marlboro, L&M, Philip Morris, Bond Street, Parliament, Chesterfield, Merit, Lark and Virginia Slims -- and including sales of recently acquired local brands in Portugal.

Broad-based volume advances were recorded around the globe, including the major markets of Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, the Benelux countries, Central and Eastern Europe, Turkey, the Middle East, Japan, Korea and Singapore, and in many other markets including the Philippines and Indonesia. Volume declined in Australia. Although volume was also down in France and Mexico, PMI's share increased in both markets.

Shares rose in virtually all major markets, with gains recorded in the important markets of Germany, Italy, Spain, the Benelux countries, Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Turkey, Japan, Korea, Singapore and Hong Kong.

The Marlboro brand, the world's most popular cigarette, continued its robust growth. The brand recorded especially strong volume gains in Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, the Benelux countries, Poland, Turkey, the Middle East, Japan and Singapore, and in the important growth markets of the Philippines and Indonesia. In addition, volume for L&M, now the world's third most popular cigarette, continued to post double-digit advances, with notable gains in Spain, the Benelux countries, Finland, Central and Eastern Europe, Turkey and the Middle East.

During the quarter, PMI continued to invest in the modernization and expansion of its manufacturing facilities in numerous countries including Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Poland, Russia, Lithuania, Ukraine, Turkey, Malaysia and Brazil.
In January 1997, PMI successfully completed its previously announced acquisition of a majority shareholding in Tabaqueira, Portugal's leading tobacco company. FOOD

Worldwide food revenues rose slightly to $7.2 billion on higher volume, partially offset by divestitures of international businesses and the adverse impact of the stronger U.S. dollar against key foreign currencies. Operating income increased 8.3%, to $1.0 billion, largely driven by volume gains.
North American Food

Kraft Foods North America (KFNA) turned in a superb quarter. Income and volume growth were outstanding, as income from operations in the U.S. and Canada reached $743 million, 10.1% higher than last year, on continued strong volume gains, higher margins and productivity savings. Operating revenues were $4.4 billion, up 7.0%.

In the United States, robust volume growth was powered by superior double-digit gains in pizza, cereals, coffee, meals, desserts and snacks, and beverages, along with strong results in cheese and meats. The high volume growth was propelled by the expansion of the successful Super Bowl mega-promotion, which linked 38 KFNA products this year; the inclusion of Taco Bell Home Originals grocery line, acquired in August 1996; heavy demand for coffee before a commodity-driven price increase; and an earlier Easter in 1997. KFNA's shares rose in each of its major categories.

The frozen pizza business had another outstanding quarter, with share up and volume increasing over 20%, driven by the continued success of Di Giorno Rising Crust pizza and the launch of Tombstone Oven Rising Crust pizza.

At the Post Cereal division, both volume and share were up strongly due to the favorable impact of the April 1996 price reduction, the successful national roll-out of Post Cranberry Almond Crunch and the relaunch of Post Frosted Shredded Wheat cereals.

In coffee, volume, share and product mix maintained their positive momentum as consumers continued to trade up to Maxwell House premium and specialty brands. However, in the coming months total coffee consumption may be sluggish as a result of the industry's higher prices at retail, which have been caused by sharp increases in coffee bean prices.

In packaged meals, Philip Morris new Light Deluxe, Cheesy Alfredo and Rugrats varieties of Kraft Macaroni & Cheese Dinners, together with the acquisition of the Taco Bell Home Originals line, drove a double-digit volume gain.

The desserts and snacks division also enjoyed double-digit volume growth, spurred by the successful launch of ready-to-eat Jell-O Cheesecake Snacks and the popularity of Del Monte Pudding Cup puddings.

The beverage business showed strong progress, with outstanding volume growth both for powdered soft drinks, led by Kool-Aid and the revitalized Tang brand, and for Kool-Aid Bursts and Capri Sun ready-to-drink beverages.

Volume at KFNA's cheese division rose strongly, led by gains in Kraft Slices and natural cheeses, and by new products including Kraft 2% Singles, Kraft Free Natural Shreds and Philly Flavors Cream Cheese.

In the processed meats division, higher volume was driven by double-digit volume growth for Oscar Mayer Lunchables lunch combinations, aided by the launch of Lunchables Deli-Carryouts sandwich products, and by gains for Slice Pak.
KFNA's salad dressing volume also showed double-digit gains, driven by effective trade and consumer promotions. However, competitive conditions in the category remain intense.

In Canada, volume was essentially flat in the branded retail business against last year's exceptionally strong results. Canadian foodservice volumes declined due to the planned elimination of low-margin products.
International Food

International food operating income of $273 million rose 3.8% over last year, on revenues of $2.8 billion, down slightly due to the impact of currency and divestitures. Earnings growth was driven by underlying volume gains in Europe and continued cost reduction, partially offset by lower earnings in Latin America.

In the coffee business of Kraft Foods International, Inc. (KFI), roast and ground shares rose in virtually all key markets, including Germany, France, Austria and Sweden. In the key German roast and ground coffee category, record shares were achieved as a result of strengthened marketing initiatives, in particular for Jacobs Kronung. In soluble coffee, KFI's share increased in the important market of the United Kingdom, as volume benefited from the growing popularity of premium-priced Carte Noire soluble coffee. Additionally, overall coffee volume was driven by strong consumer and trade demand in advance of announced price increases.

In confectionery, volume grew strongly in Germany, KFI's largest confectionery market, with good share gains for Milka, the leading chocolate tablet, bolstered by marketing programs including the highly successful World Cup Ski sponsorship in 13 European countries. In addition, volumes were also favorably impacted by the introduction of a 55-gram version of Milka Schoko & Keks in Germany and the introduction of mini tablets under the leading Cote d'Or brand in Belgium.

KFI's cheese and grocery business also registered volume gains in several markets, including Dairylea process cheese in the United Kingdom, Sottilette process cheese in Italy and Kraft salad dressings in Australia.

In its developing markets, KFI continued to make progress, with good volume gains in China. In addition, volume grew strongly in both Lithuania and the Ukraine, benefiting from the continued gains of Karuna and Korona chocolates, respectively.
During the quarter, KFI completed the sale of its Malaco sugar confectionery business in Scandinavia.

In Latin America, beverage volume grew, led by the continued strong momentum of Tang and Clight powdered soft drinks in Argentina and by Tang in Puerto Rico. Confectionery volume increased as a result of the July 1996 acquisition of the controlling interest in Industrias de Chocolate Lacta S.A. in Brazil. Ice cream sales in Brazil were down due to unseasonably cool weather and increased competition.
BEER

Miller Brewing Company had operating revenues of $986 million in the first quarter, 10.4% lower than last year, as Miller refocused its attention on its core brands. Operating income rose 2.6%, to $119 million, due to continued productivity improvements and lower costs.

Miller's shipments declined 9.0% to 10.1 million barrels due to the decision to reduce 1997 wholesaler inventories, and a difficult comparison to last year's first quarter, which witnessed the launch of Miller Beer. However, wholesalers' sales to retailers were down only slightly, primarily due to one less trading day in 1997. Sales of Miller Lite to retailers continued to grow, as did those of Miller High Life, Icehouse and the popular imported brand, Foster's.
